items.followUp: Name two basic elements used in HTML and state the purpose of each.

rubric.why: Tags identify and mark up HTML content or instructions.
rubric.description: Identifies tags as an HTML element.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming tags.

rubric.why: Attributes provide additional information about HTML elements.
rubric.description: Identifies attributes as an HTML element.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming attributes.

modelAnswer: The basic elements needed to understand HTML include tags and attributes.
Tags mark the beginning and end of HTML elements or instructions.
Attributes provide additional information about an HTML element.

items.followUp: Define an algorithm and write two advantages and two disadvantages of using one.

rubric.why: An algorithm is a finite sequence of steps for solving a problem.
rubric.description: Defines an algorithm as an ordered or finite set of steps for solving a problem.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the essential definition.

rubric.why: These are common advantages of algorithms.
rubric.description: States advantages of an algorithm.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any three valid advantages.

rubric.why: Algorithms can take time to write, become lengthy for complex problems, and be difficult to modify.
rubric.description: States disadvantages of an algorithm.
rubric.how: Award up to 2 marks for any three valid disadvantages.

modelAnswer: An algorithm is a finite sequence of well-defined steps used to solve a problem.
Advantages:
It is easy to understand and communicate.
It helps to detect errors in the solution.
It is independent of any particular programming language.
Disadvantages:
Writing an algorithm can be time-consuming.
An algorithm for a complex problem may become lengthy.
A lengthy algorithm can be difficult to modify.

items.followUp: Define data communication and name three other components of a communication system.

rubric.why: Data communication means the exchange or transfer of data between devices.
rubric.description: Defines data communication.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the exchange or transfer of data.

rubric.why: The sender or source originates and sends the message.
rubric.description: Names and describes the sender/source component.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for sender/source.

rubric.why: The receiver or destination gets the message.
rubric.description: Names and describes the receiver/destination component.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for receiver/destination.

rubric.why: The medium or channel carries the message between sender and receiver.
rubric.description: Names the transmission medium/channel component.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the medium/channel.

modelAnswer: Data communication is the exchange or transfer of data between two or more devices through a communication medium.
Three components of a communication system are:
Sender: the device or person that sends the message.
Receiver: the device or person that receives the message.
Transmission medium: the channel through which the message travels.

items.followUp: What is software piracy? Explain two forms of software piracy.

rubric.why: Software piracy is the unauthorized copying, use, or distribution of copyrighted software.
rubric.description: Defines software piracy as unauthorized use or copying of software.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the essential idea of unauthorized software use or copying.

rubric.why: Softlifting includes making unauthorized copies for use on multiple computers.
rubric.description: Explains softlifting or unauthorized copying for multiple users/devices.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct explanation of one type.

rubric.why: Counterfeit software is illegally duplicated and sold as genuine.
rubric.description: Explains counterfeit software.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct explanation of a second type.

rubric.why: Online piracy involves illegally copying, sharing, or downloading software through the internet.
rubric.description: Explains online piracy or another valid type.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct explanation of a third type.

modelAnswer: Software piracy is the unauthorized copying, use, or distribution of copyrighted software.
Three types of software piracy are:
Softlifting: making unauthorized copies of software for use on more computers than the licence permits.
Counterfeiting: illegally copying and selling software as if it were genuine.
Online piracy: illegally downloading or sharing software through the internet.

items.followUp: Write any two disadvantages of using a flowchart.

rubric.why: Preparing a flowchart can take considerable time.
rubric.description: States that drawing a flowchart is time-consuming.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this or another valid disadvantage.

rubric.why: A large or complex flowchart can be difficult to modify or may become unwieldy.
rubric.description: States another valid disadvantage of flowcharts.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a distinct valid disadvantage.

modelAnswer: Drawing a flowchart can be time-consuming.
A flowchart for a large problem can become complex and difficult to modify.

items.followUp: What is meant by a problem in problem solving?

rubric.why: A problem is a situation, condition, or difficulty that needs attention.
rubric.description: Identifies a problem as a situation or condition requiring attention.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the situation or difficulty.

rubric.why: A problem is something for which a solution or resolution is required.
rubric.description: States that a solution or resolution is required.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this essential part of the definition.

modelAnswer: A problem is a situation or difficulty that needs to be solved.
It requires a suitable solution or resolution.

items.followUp: For a valid range of 10 to 50, what boundary test values should be checked?

rubric.why: Boundary test data checks values at the limits of the valid range.
rubric.description: Identifies that boundary values or limits are tested.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for referring to the limits/boundaries of the range.

rubric.why: Testing values just below, at, and just above a boundary helps reveal boundary errors.
rubric.description: States the values to test around a boundary.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for specifying just-below, at, and just-above values.

modelAnswer: Boundary test data consists of values at the limits of the valid range and values just below and just above those limits.
For a range of 10 to 50, test values such as 9, 10, 11, 49, 50, and 51.

rubric.why: The binary digits are assigned powers of 2 according to their positions.
rubric.description: Shows the positional expansion of the binary number.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct expansion or equivalent positional values.

rubric.why: The decimal value of (10011)₂ is 19.
rubric.description: Gives the correct decimal answer.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct answer.

modelAnswer: Given: (10011)₂
